study_identification_part.si4_title: Atypical maturation of the functional connectome hierarchy in autism

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research aims and the purpose of applying normative modeling: (1) to trace the developmental trajectory of the cortical hierarchy in typically developing (TD) individuals using normative modeling, (2) to quantify individual-level deviations in ASD relative to the normative trajectory via centile scores, and (3) to assess clinical relevance and connectome-level mechanisms (mediation). These map directly to the item’s criteria.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In this study, we aimed to evaluate whether a distinct developmental trajectory reflecting an atypical cortical hierarchy exists in ASD compared with the TD group... we first applied a normative modeling approach ... to trace the development of cortical hierarchy in TD individuals... we explored whether a summary metric, the hierarchy score ... would show a distinct pattern ... Finally, we performed mediation analyses..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study uses a NEW normative model built from HCP-D (healthy TD cohort) and transferred to ABIDE TD. It specifies exclusion based on motion (mean FD ≥ 0.5 mm) and faulty cortical surface segmentation, and cites datasets and IRB/consent procedures. However, it does not explicitly report final reference sample sizes and detailed exclusion counts in the main text (these are only referenced as Supplementary Tables/figures).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"Participants with large head motion in the rs-fMRI time series (≥ 0.5 mm mean framewise displacement) and faulty cortical surface segmentation in T1-weighted (T1w) MRI were excluded (Supplementary Fig. 1)." 
"To construct a normative developmental trajectory, we used an additional cohort of 652 neurologically healthy children and adolescents from the Lifespan Human Connectome Project Development (HCP-D) dataset."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex are modeled via age and age×sex terms in GAMLSS for the reference cohort. Multi-site effects are addressed by ComBat harmonization for ABIDE gradients.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text:
"Region-wise normative modeling of gradient values based on age and the interaction between age and sex was performed... GAMLSS model fitting was implemented using the gamlss R package." 
"Finally, to mitigate scanner and site effects within the ABIDE dataset, combat [ComBat] harmonization was applied to the gradient values."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort sources are clearly described: HCP-Development (HCP-D; healthy children/adolescents) used to build the normative model, and ABIDE-I/II (TD participants) for transfer and analyses.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"Two large-scale independent datasets from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE), termed the ABIDE I and II... were analyzed." 
"To construct a normative developmental trajectory, we used an additional cohort of 652 neurologically healthy children and adolescents from the Lifespan Human Connectome Project Development (HCP-D) dataset."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data (existing datasets) were used (ABIDE I/II, HCP-D); per guidance, acquisition protocol details are not required for NA in this case.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "Two large-scale independent datasets from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE)..." / "Lifespan Human Connectome Project Development (HCP-D) dataset."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The study details preprocessing pipelines: HCP-style pipelines via QuNex for ABIDE; steps include bias-field correction, skull stripping, segmentation, MNI normalization, slice-timing and motion correction, surface mapping, 2 mm FWHM smoothing, bandpass filtering (0.008–0.1 Hz), and regression of six motion parameters; despiking and scrubbing not performed.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The ABIDE-I and II datasets were preprocessed using QuNex, which adapts HCP preprocessing pipelines... T1w data were bias-field corrected, skull stripped... BOLD time-series data were slice-timing-corrected, head-motion-corrected, and registered to the MNI space... Surface-based spatial smoothing with a 2 mm FWHM was performed... a bandpass filter 0.008–0.1 Hz was applied, and six head-motion parameters were further regressed out. Despiking and motion scrubbing were not performed."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For the NEW normative model, no explicit internal validation strategy (e.g., held-out test set, K-fold/LOOCV) for the reference cohort is described. The manuscript emphasizes transfer to ABIDE and replication, but does not report internal partitioning-based validation for healthy reference data.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No explicit cross-validation/hold-out description for reference cohort found in Methods/Results.

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model built on HCP-D was applied to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals (ABIDE TD) via transfer (intercept re-estimation), and findings were replicated using ABIDE-II.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text:
"A normative model for the gradient values was constructed using the HCP-D dataset and then transferred to the TD group of the ABIDE dataset." 
"We replicated our findings using the independent ABIDE-II dataset to verify the reproducibility."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described in detail: GAMLSS with SHASH distribution, age and age×sex terms, P-splines; implementation via the R "gamlss" package.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Normative models were constructed using the GAMLSS model... We used the four-parameter sinh–arcsinh (SHASH) distribution... Region-wise normative modeling of gradient values based on age and the interaction between age and sex... GAMLSS model fitting was implemented using the gamlss R package."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The manuscript does not report quantitative model fit/calibration metrics for the reference cohort (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage). It reports significant age effects and downstream analyses but no explicit performance metrics.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Significant age effects were determined..." (no R², error, or coverage metrics reported).

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning (train/validation/test) is reported for the NEW normative model; per guidance, answer NA when no partitioning is performed.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software/toolboxes are named (BrainSpace, BrainStat, R gamlss), and data sources and access are provided. However, specific software/library versions and code/model availability are not reported.

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "We assessed the total SRS score and five subscores..." (no mention of medication status, illness duration, or comorbidities).

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text:
